instructions.name: abort_launch
docs: Abandons a launch before any wrapper exists and returns the asset to the issuer.
Valid only at `Funded` and `Configured`. Beyond those stages buyers hold wrapper tokens
backed by the escrowed asset, and it is no longer the issuer's alone to withdraw.

accounts.name: issuer
docs: Only the issuer. Unlike settlement, this is not something a stranger should be able to
trigger: it ends a launch.

instructions.name: bridge_deposit
docs: Bridge, wrap direction: deposit the asset, receive the wrapper one for one.
Open to any approved holder. Puts a ceiling on the wrapper's market price, because a
premium can always be sold into.

accounts.name: user_crwa_account
docs: Created on demand: a first-time depositor has no wrapper account yet.

accounts.name: deposit_rule
docs: investor -> vault. Governs the incoming transfer.

accounts.name: redeem_rule
docs: vault -> investor. Not used by this transfer; checked so that nobody deposits into a
launch they could never redeem from.

instructions.name: bridge_redeem
docs: Bridge, unwrap direction: burn the wrapper, receive the asset one for one.
The protocol's compliance gate. This is the moment someone takes ownership of a regulated
security, so the redeemer's registration is verified by Aegis directly rather than left
to the token's hook. Puts a floor under the wrapper's market price.

accounts.name: user_real_rwa_account
docs: Must already exist. Registering it with Upside requires the account first, so anyone
entitled to redeem necessarily has one.

accounts.name: user_saa
docs: The redeemer's own registration. Its absence is what stops an unapproved wallet from
taking delivery of a security.

instructions.name: claim_partner_migration_fee
docs: Claims the protocol's share of the migration fee taken off the raise at graduation.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: Anyone.

instructions.name: claim_partner_trading_fee
docs: Claims the protocol's share of the bonding curve's trading fees.
Permissionless: the destination is pinned to the platform fee recipient, so a stranger
calling it only pays to move the protocol's money to the protocol.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: Anyone. Pays the transaction and any rent for the destination account.

accounts.name: aegis_crwa_account
docs: Required by Meteora's account list even though nothing is claimed into it. Pointed at the
protocol's own wrapper account rather than the treasury's, so that if a base fee ever did
arrive it would land somewhere the protocol already accounts for.

instructions.name: claim_unsold
docs: The issuer collects the asset behind their unsold wrapper, once they are a registered
holder. Pays only what the vault holds above the wrapper supply, so cRWA holders are
always covered first.

accounts.name: issuer
docs: Only the issuer. Like `abort_launch`, this moves the security to them.

accounts.name: crwa_mint
docs: Read for its supply: the part of the vault that backs the wrapper and must not be paid out.

accounts.name: issuer_saa
docs: The issuer's own holder record. To receive the security they must be registered, in the
investor group the launch was configured with, like anyone else.

instructions.name: create_rwa
docs: Launch step 1: create the Real RWA — the legal, compliance-restricted security token.
Aegis builds it so its shape is guaranteed correct, then hands the issuer all four
Upside roles. Aegis keeps no authority over the legal token.

accounts.name: issuer
docs: The asset issuer. Pays for everything and receives all four Upside roles.

accounts.name: real_rwa_mint
docs: A fresh keypair. Upside initializes the mint inside its own instruction, so this
arrives uninitialized and must sign.

accounts.name: access_control
docs: substituted account cannot be passed.

instructions.name: create_rwa_config
docs: Launch step 3: create and validate the Meteora DBC config for this launch.

accounts.name: quote_token
docs: Proof that the admin approved this quote token. Its existence is the whitelist.

accounts.name: aegis_authority
docs: Meteora overloads `fee_claimer` with four roles at once: partner fee recipient, partner
LP position owner, partner migration-fee claimant, and — with the authority option below
— cRWA mint authority. All four must therefore land on something that can sign a CPI,
which rules out a plain treasury wallet.
Derived canonically rather than from `launch.authority_bump`. The stored bump is only
written at `fund_vault`, so trusting it here would make an out-of-order call fail with an
opaque seeds error instead of naming the real problem. Nothing signs with this PDA in
this instruction — it is only recorded as Meteora's partner — so re-deriving costs a
little compute and nothing else.

accounts.name: meteora_config
docs: must sign for its own rent.

accounts.name: meteora_dbc_program
docs: their own program and have Aegis call it with the issuer as payer — and the event
authority below, being derived from whatever program is passed, would validate nothing.

accounts.name: aegis_hook_program
docs: It approves every transfer. It exists only because Meteora refuses to grant mint
authority on a non-hook config, and mint authority is what the bridge runs on.

instructions.name: finalize_graduation
docs: Launch step 5: settle the unsold allocation and open the bridge.
Collects the wrapper the curve never sold, burns it, and records the matching asset as
owed to the issuer, so total supply keeps meaning what it claims. The asset stays in the
vault, so opening the bridge never depends on the issuer being registered.
Permissionless: it squares the books and moves nothing to the caller. Must follow
Meteora's migration, which Meteora itself enforces.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: Anyone. Pays rent for the collection account and nothing else.

accounts.name: aegis_authority
docs: given at config time.

accounts.name: aegis_crwa_account
docs: Where Meteora deposits the unsold wrapper. It must be an associated token account of the
leftover receiver, and Meteora does not create it, so it is created here if missing.

accounts.name: escrow_vault
docs: Read only: its balance is the escrow side of the ledger. Nothing is moved out of it here.

accounts.name: virtual_pool
docs: Meteora refuses to release the leftover unless this shows the graduated pool already
exists, which is what orders settlement after migration.
Loaded as a typed account rather than left unchecked, because its `is_withdraw_leftover`
flag has to be read before deciding whether to call Meteora at all — see the handler.
The type also proves the pool is the transfer-hook variant this launch created.

instructions.name: fund_vault
docs: Launch step 2: lock the entire Real RWA supply in the Aegis escrow vault.
Verifies the issuer's Upside compliance setup first — in particular that the redemption
path out of the vault is open — then mints the full supply into escrow.

accounts.name: issuer
docs: Must be the issuer recorded on the launch, and must hold ReserveAdmin.

accounts.name: escrow_vault
docs: Upside's `mint_securities` requires the destination to be an associated token account of
the destination authority, so the vault address is fully determined by the launch.

accounts.name: issuer_wallet_role
docs: Proves the issuer still holds ReserveAdmin. Upside re-checks this, but failing here
gives a message that names the actual problem.

accounts.name: vault_saa
docs: The vault's holder record. Also required by `mint_securities` for any destination that
is not a registered lockup escrow — which ours is not, and cannot be.

accounts.name: redeem_rule
docs: The vault -> investor rule. Its address encodes both group ids, so passing the wrong
rule cannot pass the seed check.

instructions.name: initialize_platform
docs: Bootstraps the Aegis Protocol global singleton state.
Establishes the master admin and the protocol treasury. Callable once.

accounts.name: admin
docs: Becomes the global protocol admin, and pays rent.
Note this is first-caller-wins: nothing here proves the signer is the deployer. Handled
as deployment procedure rather than in code — initialize in the same script as the
deploy and verify `platform_config.admin` before announcing the program. See `audit.md`
finding 5.

accounts.name: platform_config
docs: The singleton PDA that stores the global protocol configuration.

instructions.name: launch_pool
docs: Launch step 4: open the sale.
Meteora creates the cRWA mint and mints the whole supply into its pool. Aegis then reads
the result back and refuses to proceed unless supply, decimals and mint authority are
exactly what the peg requires. Compute-heavy — raise the budget above the 200k default.

accounts.name: issuer
docs: The issuer. Becomes Meteora's pool creator, which carries the issuer's share of the
graduated liquidity position, their trading fees, surplus and migration fee.

accounts.name: aegis_authority
docs: what makes it the cRWA mint authority once the pool exists.

accounts.name: redeem_rule
docs: The vault -> investor rule, pinned to the groups recorded at funding so the redemption
path cannot have been quietly redirected to a different pair of groups.

accounts.name: meteora_config
docs: deserializes and validates it.

accounts.name: pool_authority
docs: pinning it costs nothing and removes an account the caller could otherwise choose.

accounts.name: crwa_mint
docs: and cannot be typed as a `Mint` until afterwards. It signs for its own rent.

accounts.name: pool
docs: substituted address fails inside their program rather than here.

accounts.name: base_vault
docs: landed in it.

accounts.name: meteora_dbc_program
docs: against this address, so without the pin none of those derivations mean anything.

accounts.name: aegis_hook_program
docs: so a mismatch here would fail inside their program too.

accounts.name: token_quote_program
docs: Quote side may be legacy SPL or Token-2022; Meteora checks it against the quote mint.

accounts.name: token_program
docs: The base side is always Token-2022.

instructions.name: update_platform_config
docs: Updates global platform parameters. Master admin only.

accounts.name: platform_config
docs: The current protocol administrator.
`has_one = admin` below ensures this signer matches the
administrator stored inside the PlatformConfig PDA.
Seeds are pinned as well as `has_one`. Only one `PlatformConfig` can exist, because
`initialize_platform` creates it at this address with `init`, so the address check is
redundant today — but every other instruction reaches the config by seeds, and leaving
one path that accepts any account of the right type is the kind of asymmetry that stops
being harmless the moment a second config becomes creatable.

accounts.name: admin
docs: The current protocol administrator who is authorized
to modify the configuration.

accounts.name: new_fee_recipient
docs: Taken as an account rather than a bare pubkey so its owner can be checked. A fee
recipient owned by another program cannot receive a plain lamport transfer, which would
make `create_rwa` fail and halt every launch until an admin noticed and changed it back.

instructions.name: update_quote_token
docs: Updates an approved quote token's status or minimum raise. Existing launches are
unaffected either way.

instructions.name: whitelist_quote_token
docs: Approves a quote token for use in launches. Protocol admin only.
Also enforces Meteora's own quote-mint rules, so an unsupported token is rejected here
rather than at pool creation, after an issuer has already locked their asset.

errors.name: UnauthorizedIssuer

errors.name: PresetInactive

errors.name: InvalidTokenStandard

errors.name: UnauthorizedTransferHook

errors.name: InvalidTotalSupply

errors.name: TokenSymbolTooLong

errors.name: TokenUriTooLong

errors.name: ComplianceRegistryMismatch

errors.name: TransfersPaused

errors.name: SupplyCapRaised

errors.name: VaultMintMismatch

errors.name: VaultNotOwnedByAegis

errors.name: VaultFrozen

errors.name: VaultHasDelegate

errors.name: VaultGroupChanged

errors.name: WrongRedeemRule

errors.name: RedemptionPathClosed

errors.name: RedemptionPathLocked

errors.name: NotLaunchIssuer

errors.name: InvalidPercentage

errors.name: CrwaMintAuthorityMismatch

fields.name: decimals
docs: Shared by the Real RWA and the cRWA. Meteora rejects anything outside 6..=9, and the
two mints must match exactly or the 1:1 backing is off by a power of ten.

fields.name: total_supply
docs: The exact supply that will be issued. Becomes Upside's `max_total_supply`, so the
issuer has no headroom to mint into without a visible on-chain cap change.

fields.name: sqrt_start_price
docs: Opening price as a Q64.64 sqrt price. Derived by the frontend from a human price; an
issuer never types this.

fields.name: sqrt_expansion_bps
docs: How far the *sqrt* price may travel over the sale, in basis points. 10_000 is flat.
Expressed against the sqrt price so no square root is needed on-chain; a sqrt multiple
of `m` is a price multiple of `m²`.

fields.name: target_raise
docs: Quote-token atoms to raise. Becomes Meteora's migration threshold.

fields.name: archetype
docs: Bounds how far the price may expand. See `curve::RwaCurveArchetype`.

fields.name: migration_fee_pct
docs: Percentage of the raise diverted out of the graduated pool at migration and paid to the
issuer and Aegis.
This is the only channel that delivers raised capital at all: Meteora turns the migration
threshold into pool liquidity, and the rest of it is locked. With this at zero an issuer
raises nothing, which is a silent and expensive surprise — hence the floor below.

fields.name: issuer_permanent_lock_pct
docs: Of the liquidity that belongs to the issuer, the share locked forever.
Permanently locked liquidity can never be withdrawn by anyone. Its fees still flow to the
issuer; the principal stays in the pool as a permanent floor under the wrapper's price.

fields.name: issuer_vested_pct
docs: Of the liquidity that belongs to the issuer, the share released on a schedule.
Together with `issuer_permanent_lock_pct` this must account for the issuer's entire
share. There is deliberately no third bucket: liquidity that is withdrawable on day one
is the exit a launchpad exists to prevent.

fields.name: vesting_months
docs: How many 30-day periods that vested share unlocks over. Must be zero when nothing vests.

fields.name: pool_fee_bps
docs: Swap fee on the graduated pool, in basis points.

fields.name: investor_group
docs: The Upside transfer group holding KYC-approved investors. The issuer chooses their own
group numbering, so Aegis cannot assume it — but it must be pinned, because redemption
is only ever permitted into this group.

fields.name: unsold_burned
docs: Unsold wrapper destroyed.

fields.name: issuer_unsold
docs: Real RWA behind that wrapper, now owed to the issuer and collectable with `claim_unsold`.

types.name: Launch
docs: Per-launch state, at PDA ["launch", real_rwa_mint].
Keyed on the Real RWA mint so that "one launch per asset" is structural, and so the
backing of a launch can be verified from a single account.

fields.name: issuer
docs: The asset issuer. Holds all four Upside roles and full legal control of the Real RWA.

fields.name: real_rwa_mint
docs: The legal, compliance-restricted token. Created by Upside via `create_rwa`.

fields.name: crwa_mint
docs: The tradable wrapper. `Pubkey::default()` until `Live` — Meteora creates it at pool init.

fields.name: meteora_config
docs: Meteora DBC config account. Default until `ConfigCreated`.

fields.name: virtual_pool
docs: Meteora DBC virtual pool. Default until `Live`.

fields.name: quote_mint
docs: Quote token for the raise (USDC). Default until `ConfigCreated`.

fields.name: escrow_vault
docs: Token-2022 account holding the Real RWA, owned by the launch's `aegis_authority` PDA.
Default until `ComplianceReady`.

fields.name: total_supply
docs: Total Real RWA to be issued, and the cRWA supply that must back it.
Equals Upside's `max_total_supply`, so there is no headroom to mint into.

fields.name: real_rwa_locked
docs: Running ledger of Real RWA held in `escrow_vault`.

fields.name: crwa_minted
docs: Running ledger of cRWA in existence.

fields.name: issuer_unsold
docs: Real RWA in the vault that belongs to the issuer, not to cRWA holders: the asset behind
the wrapper the curve never sold. Recorded by `finalize_graduation`, paid out by
`claim_unsold`.
Kept in the vault rather than sent at graduation, so opening the bridge never depends on
the issuer being registered. It is never backing for cRWA: `claim_unsold` pays only what
the vault holds above the cRWA supply, so holders are always covered first.

fields.name: vault_group
docs: Upside transfer group the escrow vault sits in. Read from the vault's holder record at
`fund_vault` and pinned from then on, so a later group change is detectable.

fields.name: investor_group
docs: Upside transfer group that KYC-approved investors sit in. Declared by the issuer at
`fund_vault`. Redemption is only permitted into this group.

fields.name: decimals
docs: Shared by both mints. Must be 6..=9 (Meteora) and identical on both sides (peg).

fields.name: archetype
docs: Set at `create_rwa_config`. Placeholder value until then.

fields.name: authority_bump
docs: Bump for ["authority", launch]. Stored so CPI signing does not re-derive it.

fields.name: migration_sqrt_price
docs: The price at which the sale actually closes, which is what the last buyer pays.

fields.name: name
docs: Metadata for the wrapper token. Cosmetic: the legal identity lives on the Real RWA.

types.name: LaunchStage
docs: How far a launch has progressed. Stages only ever move forward, and every instruction
asserts the exact stage it is valid in.
The stages exist because token genesis cannot happen in one shot: Meteora creates the cRWA
mint itself, inside its own pool-initialization instruction, so the wrapper token does not
exist until `Live`.

fields.name: kind
docs: 0 trading fee, 1 migration fee. See `instructions::claim::RevenueKind`.

types.name: PlatformConfig
docs: Global protocol settings.
Every economic field here falls into one of two groups, and the distinction matters:
* **Protocol revenue** — a single value the admin sets. The issuer cannot choose these,
because the issuer would always choose zero.
* **Bounds on issuer choices** — a floor and a ceiling. Inside them the issuer decides,
because these are choices about the issuer's own capital where different issuers
legitimately want different answers.
Anything that protects the backing or the anti-rug guarantees is not here at all. Those are
fixed in the program and neither party can move them.

fields.name: admin
docs: The global administrator of the Aegis protocol.

fields.name: fee_recipient
docs: The protocol treasury. Receives the launch creation fee and every claimed revenue stream.

fields.name: creation_fee_lamports
docs: Flat fee charged in lamports to create a launch.

fields.name: is_paused
docs: Master failsafe switch. If true, new launches revert.

fields.name: curve_fee_bps
docs: Fee charged on every trade during the sale, in basis points. This is the placement fee:
the protocol's main compensation for running the launch. Meteora's own floor is 25 bps.

fields.name: issuer_curve_fee_share_pct
docs: The issuer's share of that placement fee, as a percentage.
Zero by default, and deliberately so. The issuer is already paid by the sale proceeds;
handing them part of the fee buyers pay to buy the issuer's own token is charging twice.
In a traditional placement the agent takes the fee and the issuer takes the proceeds.

fields.name: aegis_migration_fee_share_pct
docs: The protocol's share of the migration fee, as a percentage.
Previously this was passed in by the issuer, which meant any issuer could set it so the
protocol received nothing. It is protocol revenue and belongs here.
Zero by default, so the fee model is a single legible number: the protocol charges the
placement fee above and nothing else. Raise it if that proves too little.

fields.name: aegis_lp_share_pct
docs: Share of the graduated liquidity permanently locked to the protocol, as a percentage.
This is the only liquidity that stays permanently. Its purpose is not anti-rug — the
bridge already guarantees redemption — but to ensure a trading venue never disappears
entirely for holders who have not completed KYC and therefore cannot use the bridge.

fields.name: min_migration_fee_pct
docs: Floor on the share of the raise paid out as cash. At zero the issuer raises nothing,
because everything they raised becomes pool liquidity.

fields.name: max_migration_fee_pct
docs: Ceiling on the same. The remainder seeds the trading venue, so this bounds how thin that
venue can be.

fields.name: min_issuer_permanent_pct
docs: Minimum share of the issuer's liquidity that must be locked permanently rather than
vested. Zero by default: vesting already prevents a day-one withdrawal, and permanently
locking a claim on a real asset is a genuine loss rather than a formality.

fields.name: min_vesting_months
docs: Bounds on how long the issuer's liquidity vests back to them, in months. The floor
protects early holders from the market emptying immediately; the ceiling stops an issuer
from tying up their own capital longer than Meteora permits.

fields.name: min_pool_fee_bps
docs: Bounds on the trading fee of the graduated pool, in basis points.
Worth keeping low. A cRWA should trade close to the value of the asset behind it, and a

types.name: QuoteToken
docs: An admin-approved quote token, at PDA ["quote_token", mint].
Existence of this account is the whitelist: no account, no launch. Keyed on the mint rather
than held as a list inside `PlatformConfig` so the set can grow without reallocating, and so
checking one costs a single account read.
Approval is not only a business decision. Meteora refuses quote mints it cannot handle
permissionlessly, so the check that happens at approval time is also the check that stops an
issuer from configuring a launch that Meteora would reject halfway through.

fields.name: decimals
docs: Copied at approval so callers do not need to load the mint to reason about amounts.

fields.name: is_active
docs: Whether new launches may use this token. Deactivating is preferred over closing the
account: launches already configured against this quote token keep working, and the
address cannot be re-approved with different data behind an operator's back.

fields.name: is_legacy_spl
docs: True when the mint is owned by the legacy SPL Token program rather than Token-2022.
Client-facing only: the program never reads it, because Meteora validates the quote token
program against the mint itself during pool creation. It is recorded so a frontend can
build the launch transaction without a second account fetch.

fields.name: min_raise
docs: Smallest raise permitted in this token, in its own smallest units.
Held per token rather than globally because the number is meaningless without the
token's decimals: a million units of a six-decimal stablecoin is a dollar, and of a
nine-decimal token it is a thousandth of one.

fields.name: approved_at
docs: Unix timestamp of approval. Useful for audit trails; never read by the program.

types.name: RwaCurveArchetype
docs: Which price-expansion ceiling the curve must respect. See the math firewall.

fields.name: remaining
docs: Still owed to the issuer. Non-zero only if the vault held less than they were owed.

fields.name: admin

fields.name: is_paused

fields.name: curve_fee_bps
docs: Placement fee on the sale, in basis points. Meteora's own floor is 25.

fields.name: issuer_curve_fee_share_pct
docs: The issuer's share of that placement fee.

fields.name: aegis_migration_fee_share_pct
docs: The protocol's share of the migration fee.
